core.title: Keep train sequences strictly linear; model new paths as new trains
core.when: you author or change any train sequence (e.g. adding steps, or when the flow seems to need a loop, a route, a branch or an alternative path)
core.then: Keep the train's sequence strictly linear (steps only, no loops, routes or branching) and express every new path as a new train.
prefer: Model each new or alternative path as its own new linear train instead of a loop, route or branch inside the existing sequence
Number steps sequentially with no gaps (1, 2, 3, …)
Give every step exactly one from and exactly one to
avoid: Adding loop or route sequence elements to a train
Encoding branching through a step with multiple from/to targets
Leaving gaps in step numbering after inserting or removing steps
core.why: Linearity is the no-loops/no-routes/no-branching rule for train sequences: sequences contain steps only, and new paths MUST become new trains rather than variations inside one sequence.
evidence: The train sequence contains only step elements — no loop or route elements
Step numbers are contiguous with no gaps
Each step has exactly one from and exactly one to
Any new or alternative path introduced by the plan exists as its own new train
verification: The check enforces three constraints on every train sequence: loop and route sequence elements are forbidden; sequential step numbering must have no gaps; each step has exactly one from and one to.

Train specification files are identifiable as plan artifacts of the train-specification kind in the plan tree, which is why the file-kind fact is observable now; the rule fixes no recognition mechanism of its own.

Observing the 'change' facts (a train sequence added or modified, a sequence element other than a step added, step numbering changed, a step's from/to changed) requires a diff-level parser of the train sequence; without such an observer, only the file-kind, operation and task-term facts are observable.

What the check does not decide on its own: whether a planned flow introduces a loop/route construct, branching, or a new/alternative path that must become a new train is a design judgement; steps written out explicitly one after another in a linear sequence are not by themselves a finding.
Scope of the check: train specifications only. Edits to train metadata outside the sequence (title, description) without touching steps, and plan artifacts that are not trains, are out of scope.

values: sequence element other than a step added

fires: Planner authors a new train, including an ordinary linear step sequence (numbering and from/to cardinality still apply)
Planner creates a new train to carry an alternative path split out of another train
Planner inserts, removes or reorders steps in an existing train
Planner adds a loop or route element to a train sequence
Planner models an alternative/error path inside an existing train instead of a new train
Train steps are renumbered leaving a gap (e.g. step 1, 2, 4)
A step declares more than one from or more than one to, or omits one
doesNotFire: Editing train metadata outside the sequence (title, description) without touching steps
Planning artifacts that are not trains (e.g. wagons, WMBTs, acceptances) with no train sequence change

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role; the core's 'train specification' file kind must be among them so the file-kind activation fact can be observed.

classification.note: Neutral: the train is a cross-stack plan artifact; no stack, path or suffix named.
Kept verbatim; train-spec vocabulary, not stack idioms.
Constraint stated generically in core.verification[0]; no detector/validator/finding ids are declared.
The 'linearity' term definition is identical to the core why.
Neutral file-kind fact kept in the core; its recognition note is carried generically in core.verification[1]; the concrete kind value comes from roles.plan_artifact.kinds.

neutralityNotes: The rule governs a plan artifact and the Bun sidecar names no stack, runtime, language, suffix or path, so the core is essentially verbatim and bunOnly is empty. Train, step, loop/route, from/to and sibling plan artifacts (wagon, WMBT, acceptance) are neutral ATDD plan vocabulary (the closed vocabulary lists them as cross-stack urn artifacts). Round 4 fixes: the stack name was removed from core.verification[1]; the roles.plan_artifact.kinds bunValue is now the exact string value 'train specification'. Recognition mechanics (role assignment, plan path, plan-artifact suffixes) are not populated by the Bun sidecar, so no values are invented for them. No per-rule disposition is declared in the Bun sidecar, so none is invented.
